_comment: Metalstorm native JS UI manifest (PLAN-native-ui.md §3). Widgets receive a ui-store read API, a DOM mount inside #ui-root, and the validated command/directive submission API. Panel CHROME (frame, header, collapse toggle, count badge) is built by the loader from the `title`/`collapsible`/`collapsed` fields below — widgets render content only, so every panel looks the same by construction.
_retired: objectives-panel — folded into the top-centre `objective-hud` (U1, DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §7). Its 5-entry outcome log is superseded by the rung-4 Events tab (U3); its bounty FORM is still homeless and still has no wire target (`objectives.createBounty`), which is why the widget file stays on disk unmounted.  command-composer — RETIRED by U4 (DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §7). `[VERB][SUBJECT][TARGET][WHEN]` chips plus a priority slider is the spreadsheet the design directive names: a four-slot form for issuing one order. It is replaced by two things that landed first — rung-3 actions on the thing itself (U0/U1: Halt, Follow, Assign to AI) and the command line's sentence, which reads the same compile table through the same envelope. client/src/native-widgets/command-composer.js stays on disk, unmounted, with its suite green: it is the only surface that can draw a ROUTE target (`nl-resolver.ts` refuses route verbs by name and points at it), so re-homing that map arm as a rung-3 action is the work that would let the file be deleted.
_layout: BOTH RAILS ARE EMPTY and so is the BOTTOM (U3+U4, DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §6/§7). Docking keeps the centre and lower-centre of the viewport clear for unit selection and orders: authority pill top-left; the drill-down chip stacks (focus + objectives) top-centre; the ONE global access point top-right, with the decaying battle notices under it. Statistics, reports, events, objectives and diplomacy live behind the access point as `mount: "menu:<tab>"` — a widget has exactly one mount, which is how §6's rule 'if a surface is in the tab strip it is not also a rail panel' is enforced by construction rather than by anyone remembering it. bottom-center holds only the summonable command line, which is absent from the DOM until `/` is pressed. Bottom-left and bottom-right belong to the engine HUD (selection readout, minimap).

widgets._chrome: No title — the pill renders its own compact frame; a header would double its height for no extra information.

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from the client bundle (client/src/ui/native-ui/focus-hud.ts) via BUILTIN_WIDGETS — it IS the drill-down framework (focus model + drilldown primitive + camera travel), which are engine modules, so there is no game-dir copy.
widgets._chrome: NO title on purpose: the loader only builds panel chrome for titled widgets, and a summary affordance must not read as a panel that lives here. The widget renders nothing at all while the selection is empty (DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §4 rung 1).

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from the client bundle (client/src/ui/native-ui/objective-hud.ts) via BUILTIN_WIDGETS — it is built on the drill-down framework (focus model + drilldown primitive + camera travel), which are engine modules, so there is no game-dir copy.
widgets._chrome: NO title, like focus-hud: interaction story 2 is a stack of rung-1 summary affordances, not a panel that lives in a rail. Nothing is in the DOM while the board is empty.
widgets._replaces: objectives-panel, removed from the right rail by the same change (DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §7 'DEMOTE to rung 1 + 2'). The panel was a resident list plus a bounty FORM beside the viewport, and it rendered the type tag 'control' where the player needed 'Hold Raven Basin'. Its live 'Assign to AI' action moved onto the objective it is about; its bounty form and 5-entry outcome log are rung-4 content and are U3's to re-home. widgets/objectives-panel.js and ui/lib/objectives.js are kept on disk with that note in their headers, unmounted, until U3 lands the rung-4 Objectives tab.

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from the client bundle (client/src/ui/native-ui/moment-hud.ts) via BUILTIN_WIDGETS — it reads the worker's battle-moment stream and the shared notice lane, both engine modules.
widgets._chrome: NO title: these are decaying notices, not a panel. Nothing is in the DOM until something happens, and every notice leaves on its own. Docked under the access point so top-centre stays the chip stacks' — DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §4.

widgets.title: Parley
widgets._chrome: Collapsed by default and badged with the incoming-proposal count — diplomacy is episodic, so the panel should announce itself rather than occupy the rail permanently.

widgets.title: AI Command
widgets._chrome: The tallest panel in the HUD (stance, ROE, region paint, asset locks, funding, intent, change feed) — set-and-forget, so it starts collapsed.

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from client/src/ui/native-ui/moment-hud.ts's `eventLog` export — the notices and the log render the same BattleMoment records through the same phrasing, so they share a module by construction.
widgets.title: Battle log

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from client/src/ui/native-ui/objective-hud.ts's `objectiveBoard` export — the full board and the top-centre chips are one reading of one wire format.
widgets.title: All objectives

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from client/src/ui/native-ui/briefing-panel.ts. The scenario story, its field advice and the par clock — all of which existed only on the boot splash and were dropped the moment the player clicked Begin.
widgets.title: Briefing

widgets._builtin_note: Mounted from the client bundle (client/src/native-widgets/command-console.js) via BUILTIN_WIDGETS — same reason as the composer: it depends on bundled native-ui modules (console-exchange + free-text-accelerator + class-vocabulary + named-entity-index). There is no game-dir copy.
widgets._chrome: PLAN-metalstorm-command-language.md §4 + DESIGN-DRILLDOWN.md §7 — the natural-language command line. NO title on purpose: a titled widget gets loader panel chrome, and a permanent "Command ▾" header at bottom-centre is exactly the resident panel §7 files this widget under DEMOTE for. It is SUMMONED with `/` (Esc dismisses) and puts nothing in the DOM until it is, so the resting HUD has no trace of it. `nlAliases` still live here: the widget exposes open/close/isOpen and the loader registers THOSE under these names (widget-loader `registerSummonActions`), so a game's panel names stay in one file.
